newsitem.title: USA: AOL faces yet another class action lawsuit.
newsitem.headline: AOL faces yet another class action lawsuit.

text.p: America Online Inc. faces yet another class action lawsuit prompted by its recent network access problems, this time seeking damages in excess of $100 million, attorneys for the plaintiffs said Thursday.

Bruce Fishelman of Standbury & Fishelman Inc. in Los Angeles said his law firm filed suit under the Racketeering Influence and Corrupt Organisation Act, alleging that AOL violated the public interest in connection with its online services.
AOL has been hit with numerous lawsuits since it switched its members to unlimited access last December and its network could not support the deluge of members seeking access.

The latest suit, filed in federal court in Los Angeles, will seek to prevent AOL from failing to protect the privacy and intellectual property rights of its members who post their own content, messages, or art on AOL.
FIshelmen said the suit is filed on behalf of AOL's more than eight million members.
An America Online spokeswoman said the Dulles, Va.-based company has not yet been served with the suit, but said it has no merit.
